name: Ghana
genZNote: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule (1957) — Kwame Nkrumah's declaration became the spark that lit the entire continent's decolonisation wave over the following decades.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in West Africa on the Gulf of Guinea, bordered by Côte d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso, and Togo.
Features tropical coastal plains, forested regions in the south, and savanna in the north, with Lake Volta — one of the world's largest artificial lakes — as a major feature.
Historically known as the 'Gold Coast' during the colonial era, reflecting its significant gold resources.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: English is the official language, alongside numerous indigenous languages including Akan, Ewe, and Ga, reflecting Ghana's ethnic diversity.
Known for vibrant Kente cloth weaving, a traditional textile with deep cultural and historical significance, alongside rich drumming and dance traditions.
A significant site of historical memory around the transatlantic slave trade, with coastal forts like Cape Coast Castle serving as major heritage and reconciliation tourism sites.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A presidential republic and one of Africa's most stable multi-party democracies, with regular peaceful transfers of power since the 1990s.
The first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule, in 1957, under founding leader Kwame Nkrumah, inspiring a wave of decolonisation across the continent.
Known as the 'Gold Coast' under British colonial rule before adopting the name Ghana at independence, referencing the ancient Ghana Empire.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A regional leader in public health initiatives, including successful national health insurance scheme models studied by other developing nations.
Growing technology and fintech startup ecosystem in Accra, alongside traditional strengths in agricultural science (cocoa research).
Historic gold and, more recently, oil (offshore Jubilee field) extraction industries underpin significant portions of scientific and engineering investment.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A founding member of the Organisation of African Unity (predecessor to today's African Union) and a symbol of pan-Africanism under Kwame Nkrumah's leadership.
Widely regarded as one of the most politically stable democracies in West Africa, playing an active role in regional peacekeeping and mediation.
An active member of ECOWAS, promoting West African regional economic integration.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Ghana maintain warm relations dating to the shared Non-Aligned Movement era, with Ghana being one of India's key West African trade and development partners.
India has extended significant lines of credit to Ghana for infrastructure, agriculture, and rural electrification projects.
Growing Indian private investment in Ghana's pharmaceutical, automotive assembly, and agro-processing sectors.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: One of the world's largest producers and exporters of cocoa, alongside significant gold and, more recently, offshore oil production.
A growing West African hub for technology and financial services, alongside traditional agricultural export strength.
Historically known for the 'Gold Coast' name reflecting centuries of gold trade significance.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being the first sub-Saharan African nation to gain independence (1957).
Being one of the world's top cocoa producers.
Kente cloth and vibrant traditional textile heritage.
Historic coastal slave-trade forts, now major heritage tourism and reconciliation sites.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Ghana is a stable West African presidential republic and multi-party democracy, the first sub-Saharan African nation to gain independence, and a top global cocoa producer.
keyFacts: Presidential republic; one of Africa's most stable multi-party democracies.
First sub-Saharan African country to gain independence, in 1957, under Kwame Nkrumah.
One of the world's largest cocoa producers.
commonConfusion: Ghana was called the 'Gold Coast' under British colonial rule — it adopted the name 'Ghana' at independence in 1957, referencing the ancient, historically unrelated Ghana Empire further north.

highYieldFacts: Ghana: presidential republic, capital Accra, first sub-Saharan African nation to gain independence (1957).
Top global cocoa producer; formerly known as the 'Gold Coast'.
India-Ghana: Non-Aligned Movement-era ties; India extends development credit lines for infrastructure and agriculture.
commonTraps: Assuming the modern nation of Ghana is a direct continuation of the ancient Ghana Empire — the name was adopted symbolically at independence.
Overlooking Ghana's reputation as one of Africa's most stable democracies when discussing regional political stability.
mustRemember: Ghana: first sub-Saharan African independence (1957), stable democracy, top cocoa producer, longstanding India development partner.
